output.contract_title: Software License Agreement with Enterprise Partner 028 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Vendor must notify customer of any security breach within 48 hours of discovery.
mandatory_requirements.compliance_check: Verify timestamped breach detection and notification logs; ensure notification is sent within 48 hours of discovery.

mandatory_requirements.description: Data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256.
mandatory_requirements.compliance_check: Inspect network configurations for TLS 1.3 usage; review storage encryption settings for AES-256 algorithm and key length.

ambiguities_in_policy.issue: Definition of "discovery" is not specified – could be interpreted as detection by vendor, internal monitoring, or third‑party reporting.
Scope of "data at rest" is unclear – does it include backups, archives, and temporary files? Also no guidance on key management or rotation for AES-256.

mappings.notes: Payment terms clause does not relate to any listed data protection policy requirements.
Vendor must notify within 24 hours, which meets the 48‑hour breach notification requirement.
Liability cap clause is unrelated to data protection requirements.
Termination clause does not address any of the specified policy requirements.
Renewal provision is not relevant to the data protection policy requirements.

deviations.supporting_evidence: Clause mappings show no clause linked to REQ-SEC-02. All existing clauses (PAY, LIAB, TERM, REN) are marked as unrelated to data protection, and the only data‑protection clause (CLS-0028-DATA) addresses breach notification, not encryption. Consequently, the contract provides no assurance that data will be encrypted in transit with TLS 1.3 or at rest with AES‑256.
deviations.recommended_remediation: Add a dedicated data‑encryption clause (e.g., CLS-0028-ENC) that explicitly requires: • All data in transit to be protected using TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy. • All data at rest to be encrypted using AES‑256 with keys managed per industry‑standard key‑management practices. Include compliance verification steps such as periodic security audits and provision of encryption configuration reports.

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is undefined and provides no mechanism for handling disputed invoices. No interest or penalty for late payment is specified, creating a one‑sided advantage for the Vendor.

"Becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach" is ambiguous; it is unclear when a breach is considered "confirmed" and what level of awareness triggers the 24‑hour notice requirement. The requirement to notify "in writing" may be impractical in emergency situations.

Limiting aggregate liability to the total fees paid in the preceding twelve months may be insufficient to cover consequential or regulatory damages, especially for the Customer. The cap is symmetric but disproportionately protects the Vendor from larger exposure.
Termination for convenience with only a 30‑day notice can cause abrupt service disruption. No transition, hand‑over, or wind‑down obligations are defined, exposing the Customer to operational risk.

Automatic annual renewal without explicit price adjustment or review provisions may lead to unintended continuation of the agreement at outdated terms. The notice period for non‑renewal is the same for both parties, but the lack of clarity on renewal pricing creates financial uncertainty.

inconsistencies.description: Termination for convenience allows either party to end the Agreement with 30 days prior written notice at any time, while the renewal provision requires a 30‑day notice of non‑renewal prior to the renewal date. The overlapping 30‑day notice periods can create ambiguity about whether a termination notice supersedes a renewal notice, leading to a potential chronological conflict.
